questions.stem: Which part of a plant grows upward in response to sunlight?
questions.solution: The shoot of a plant grows upward in response to sunlight. This is because shoots exhibit phototropism, which is the growth toward a light source. Roots grow downward due to gravitropism, leaves do not typically grow in a specific direction in response to light, and flowers can grow in various directions depending on the species.

hi.solution: एक पौधे की कली सूर्य के प्रकाश के प्रति ऊपर की ओर बढ़ती है। इसका कारण यह है कि कलियाँ प्रकाशगति के अनुरूप बढ़ती हैं, जो एक प्रकाश स्रोत की ओर बढ़ने की प्रक्रिया है। जड़ें गुरुत्वाकर्षण के कारण नीचे की ओर बढ़ती हैं, पत्तियाँ आमतौर पर प्रकाश के प्रति कोई विशिष्ट दिशा में बढ़ती नहीं हैं, और फूल जाति के आधार पर विभिन्न दिशाओं में बढ़ सकते हैं।
hi.critique: The Hindi translation accurately reflects the English content with appropriate botanical terminology.

questions.stem: In which direction does the shoot grow when sunlight is provided from only one direction?
questions.solution: When sunlight comes from only one direction, the shoot grows upwards towards the light due to phototropism. This is a natural response where plants grow toward the source of light. The other options are incorrect because the shoot does not grow downward, nor does it spread in all directions, and while it may bend slightly, its primary direction is upward.

hi.stem: जब केवल एक दिशा से सूर्य का प्रकाश प्रदान किया जाता है, तो शूट किस दिशा में बढ़ता है?
hi.solution: जब सूर्य का प्रकाश केवल एक दिशा से आता है, तो शूट प्रकाश की ओर ऊपर की ओर बढ़ता है क्योंकि यह प्रकाशगति के कारण होता है। यह एक प्राकृतिक प्रतिक्रिया है जहां पौधे प्रकाश के स्रोत की ओर बढ़ते हैं। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि शूट नीचे की ओर नहीं बढ़ता है, न ही यह सभी दिशाओं में फैलता है, और यद्यपि यह थोड़ा झुक सकता है, तो इसकी प्राथमिक दिशा ऊपर की ओर होती है।

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common feature between the life cycles of a mosquito and a frog?
choices: They both have four stages in their life cycle
They both lay their eggs in water
They both have a pupal stage
They both develop from a seed
questions.solution: Both mosquitoes and frogs lay their eggs in water, which is a common feature of their life cycles. The other options are incorrect because not all stages are the same, and neither develops from a seed. Mosquitoes have a pupal stage, but frogs do not. Neither has four identical stages, though both have four distinct stages.

questions.stem: What is the main reason mosquito larvae and pupae come to the surface of the water?
questions.solution: Mosquito larvae and pupae need to breathe air, so they come to the surface of the water to access oxygen. They do not come to the surface to find food, escape predators, or lay eggs, as these activities occur elsewhere in the water. Their primary need at the surface is for respiration.

questions.stem: If a student observes a stage in a water body that has a tail and no legs, which stage of the frog's life cycle is it most likely to be?
questions.solution: A tadpole is the stage of a frog's life cycle that has a tail and no legs, which matches the observation in the question. Adult frogs have legs, froglets have both legs and a tail, and eggs are not developed enough to have a tail or legs. Therefore, the correct answer is tadpole.
